app.title: NIUCHACZ {version} – POST card diagnostics
calib.applied: Saved. Codes are now decoded with the new map.
calib.auto_close: Variants too close ({best} vs {second}) – collect more frames (more board starts) or add a steady text.
calib.auto_ok: Automatic: {best} of digits readable (next variant {second}). Channels {pairs}{note}. Click "Apply".
calib.conflict: No result – the typed readings contradict each other; click Clear.
calib.err_chars: The text may contain only 0-9, A-F, '-' and space
calib.err_dup: The same line state was already saved as "{text}". The card has not changed yet or the reading is stale – wait until the text on the card is steady and try again.
calib.err_few: Not enough data ({n} frames). Restart the board 2–3 times with NIUCHACZ connected and try again.
calib.err_no_data: No data from NIUCHACZ – connect first.
calib.help:
Legacy method – only for cards read through the 7-segment display.

1. Connect to NIUCHACZ and wait until the card shows a steady text (e.g. the board waits for F1 or is in Setup).
2. Type exactly what you see on the card (4 characters, from the left) and click "Add reading".
3. Usually 2–3 different texts are enough. When the result is unambiguous, click "Apply".

Codes change too fast? Type one steady text (e.g. from the BIOS menu), restart the board 2–3 times and click "Automatic" – the program will work out the rest from the recorded frames.
calib.many: {n} variants match – add another reading with different digits (ideally a different digit in each position, no 8).
calib.none: No matching assignment – check the text and the wires.

calib.unique: Unambiguous: channels {pairs}; digits from the left = lines {lines}; a segment is lit at {level} level.
